findings.title: Rendering a small DOCX table can exhaust host memory
findings.summary:
An untrusted DOCX author can set huge positive w:gridSpan, w:gridBefore or w:gridAfter counts in a small, shallow table. Rendering sums those counts into grid occupancy and directly sizes column, preference and merge vectors. Counts of 1000000000/1073741824 request about 4 GB/4 GiB for f32 columns; 4294967295 requests approximately 16 GiB before additional allocations, despite package admission. Assigned discovery-0031 corroborates the existing one-billion-column, 4,000,000,000-byte f32-vector framing through both span and row-skip inputs; these are static counts.
 Assigned discovery-0032 corroborates the live span and both synthetic row-skip paths, including merge-slot expansion; separate Markdown span clamping does not protect rendering.
findings.remediation:
Enforce practical per-span and total-column budgets for gridSpan, gridBefore and gridAfter before excessive RawCell, column, preference or merge allocation/work. Use checked occupancy sums and col+span arithmetic, apply the same budget to every derived table vector, and return a typed resource-limit refusal on excess. Propagate a caller-adjustable semantic column limit through all public rendering surfaces and charge later column/merge vectors to that same budget.
Additional retained remediation detail: Enforce explicit maximum live cell spans, row skips, aggregate table columns and merge slots before any allocation. Use checked sums and a cumulative layout resource budget, returning a typed refusal when exceeded.

findings.title: Large Chicago numbering values can exhaust memory while reading or rendering a DOCX
findings.summary:
An untrusted DOCX can select Chicago numbering with a huge list start/startOverride or section page start. The shared chicago_label formatter repeats a UTF-8 symbol roughly n/4 times without a length bound, allowing gigabyte allocations during list rendering, ordinary section-page processing and Markdown numbered-list views. Authored endnote starts also reach this shared formatter. The supplied u32::MAX framing selects 1073741824 double-daggers, about 3 GiB of UTF-8 label bytes; this is static arithmetic. Additional supplied static framing: start=2147483647 selects 536870912 UTF-8 double-daggers (‡), requesting 1.5 GiB of marker bytes before downstream copies.
 Assigned discovery-0032 additionally supplies start=4294967294: 1073741824 daggers (†), about 3 GiB of UTF-8 before copies. Level-zero reader/agent labels reach the shared formatter without a large ilvl.
findings.remediation:
Bound generated byte/glyph length inside the shared Chicago formatter before repetition, with a documented safe cycle/fallback or typed refusal. Apply that bound to all list, startOverride, section-page and Markdown/direct list_number callers; do not rely on input bytes, counter saturation or later clipping. Include authored endnote numStart/format and MCP agent-view callers in the shared formatter budget.
Additional retained remediation detail: Apply a central maximum output length to Chicago labels before repetition and enforce a cumulative numbering-output budget. Use a documented bounded fallback or typed refusal consistently for list, read/agent, page and future formatter consumers.

findings.title: Rendering an HTML chunk can allocate gigabytes from a single colspan value
findings.summary:
A document author can place a huge positive colspan in a small embedded HTML/MHT altChunk table. Ordinary DOCX rendering generates one grid XML element per effective column after original package admission and before DOM/layout checks. A count of 1000000000 drives a billion appends; 4294967295 generates over 85 GB of markup, exhausting CPU/memory. The supplied positive 4294967295 framing fits both 32-bit and 64-bit usize and needs no arithmetic overflow. Assigned discovery-0031 corroborates colspan=1000000000 causing tens of gigabytes of generated XML and work before layout; rejecting invalid, negative or zero spans does not bound valid positive values.
 Assigned discovery-0032 supplies a static colspan=1000000000 framing of one billion 20-byte grid elements, about 20 GB of generated text before DOM construction; this is not a runtime measurement.
findings.remediation:
Enforce a practical maximum cell span and checked per-row/aggregate column counts before generating any table XML. Charge all HTML/MHT-generated WML, including repeated/nested tables, to a cumulative byte/work budget inside altChunk expansion and return a typed input-limit refusal before allocation or DOM construction.
Additional retained remediation detail: Bound individual spans and aggregate columns before summation or iteration, use checked arithmetic, and impose a cumulative generated-WML byte/element budget shared across every HTML/MHT altChunk. Refuse excessive expansion with a typed input-limit error before allocation.

findings.title: WMF record-boundary failures amplify polygon work and retained text
findings.summary: Rendering a DOCX with a crafted placeable WMF lets short declared records consume payload from later records, which the outer parser then revisits. Polygon/polypolygon/polyline records can cause billions of coordinate decodes from roughly 512 KiB; EXTTEXTOUT/TEXTOUT records can retain hundreds of megabytes of overlapping owned strings from roughly 205.6 KB. The common missing record-local boundary bypasses the canvas cap and original package budgets. A further framing uses alternating six-byte EXTTEXTOUT and unknown 0xFFFF record headers to claim 65,535 text bytes from subsequent records, implying several GiB of retained strings from roughly 1 MiB of media; this is a static estimate. A supplied 7-word EXTTEXTOUT framing uses 65536 fourteen-byte records plus a 65535-byte suffix in less than 1 MiB and requests about 4 GiB of decoded characters; nonzero mapping dimensions and nonblank text are required. This is a static estimate. Assigned discovery-0031 supplies an additional static eight-byte TEXTOUT framing with a 65535-byte claimed string and overlapping following bytes. About 1 MiB can request multiple gigabytes of retained text; valid whole-file reads, nonblank text and nonzero mapping extents remain required. No out-of-bounds memory read is asserted.
findings.remediation: Confine every WMF handler, including field, font, string and geometry reads, to a slice limited to its checked declared record extent. Before allocation validate fixed fields, ring/point counts and coordinate arrays, EXTTEXTOUT options/optional rectangle and text count, and TEXTOUT padded string plus trailing coordinates against that slice using checked arithmetic. Refuse inconsistent records before decoding/rasterization/replay and enforce cumulative decoded-text, record and total geometry/work budgets. Keep the already bounded EMF behavior.

findings.title: ZIP footer and count interpretation mismatch bypasses entry-count admission
findings.summary: The independent preindex footer parser can count a different EOCD or count field from zip 9.0.5. False small-count EOCDs in valid comments can be skipped by zip; a same-footer total=3/on-this-disk=10001 also passes max_entries=10000 while zip indexes 10001. ZIP64 size/offset triggers differ too. Neither admission nor PartFs enforces the actual opened count; duplicate detection also trusts the unrelated declared count. Another supplied false-footer proof uses an EOCD-shaped record inside the real archive comment whose own comment length is impossible; preindex trusts its low count while the ZIP reader rejects it and backtracks.
findings.remediation: Use the delegated reader's authoritative validated EOCD/ZIP64 selection, consistent ZIP32 total/per-disk fields and all ZIP64 total/size/offset triggers. Bound raw central-record traversal/count before index allocation, reject inconsistent unsupported metadata, and retain a post-open active archive.len cap as defense in depth; that later check cannot undo earlier allocation. Reconcile selected raw counts with indexed counts for exact duplicates, including name collapse, comments, ZIP64 and prepended data. Detect raw exact-name duplicates directly or through the reader's duplicate flag rather than relying solely on a count-shortfall inference.

findings.title: Redaction succeeds while UTF-16 XML retains the removed text
findings.summary: The redact operation can return successful clean and redline documents while a supported BOM-marked UTF-16LE/BE auxiliary XML part still contains the same confidential text. Its XML leak branch uses lossy UTF-8 and misses the retained copy, which a recipient can recover after sharing. Even the scanner's no-root fallback searches the already lossily decoded string, so it cannot recover a multi-character value split by UTF-16 NUL bytes.
findings.remediation: Decode every XML part with the same BOM-aware policy as admission before semantic leak scanning. Fail closed on unsupported/undecodable/unparseable representations and retain raw UTF8 and both UTF16 byte-order checks as defense in depth. Use the same decoding across leak checks and package validation.

findings.title: Metadata scrub leaves property parts under alternate names
findings.summary: With docprops enabled, scrub removes metadata only from three conventional filenames. A document using alternate package relationship targets can retain creators, editors, dates, company/manager or custom properties while scrub returns success. The custom-properties branch additionally skips relationship/content-type removal when docProps/custom.xml is absent, leaving an active relationship to a relocated target such as metadata/private.xml.
findings.remediation: Resolve all core, extended and custom property parts through authoritative package relationships and content types, sanitize every applicable internal target according to docprops selection, and remove corresponding custom-property parts/relationships/content-type records coherently. Verify the selected privacy postcondition; refuse unsupported or ambiguous layouts rather than returning a successfully scrubbed copy. Preserve intentional title/subject/application and revision-date retention. Missing/invalid selected targets require explicit refusal or documented safe handling; default public and CLI callers must enforce the same postcondition. Include supported Strict property relationship variants and regression cases containing both conventional and relocated targets; every active property target must satisfy the requested postcondition.

findings.title: Python CLI output/plan and npm direct-output symlinks can overwrite unrelated files
findings.summary:
Python and npm ordinary-output helpers check pathname existence separately from truncating writes; a local writer of the selected directory can replace an output name and redirect generated bytes to a victim-writable file. Python plan recording additionally uses a predictable basename/PID partial pathname without exclusive creation. The assigned report also corroborates npm plan staging, which is represented by the separately retained symlink-following.plan-staging finding. Without --force, a stable symlink to an existing referent is refused; post-preflight substitution bypasses that refusal, and a dangling link can pass the existence test. Filesystem/OS protections and shared-directory authority remain prerequisites. The shared writers also publish read/compare/revision results, document/PDF/PNG and font/render products, edit/visual-diff bundles, field-update reports, and repair outputs. Assigned Python and npm diff/bundle traces explicitly include dangling destination links permitting unintended file creation without --force, and forced existing-member links redirecting bundle/report writes; stable existing referents are refused in the ordinary nonracing no-force case.
 Assigned discovery-0032 corroborates Python PDF/PNG publication and Node renderTo, with conversion between existence preflight and final write; shared mutable directory entries and distinct attacker/victim authority remain essential.
findings.remediation:
Publish Python/Node ordinary outputs, bundles and reports through held-directory authority and exclusive private staging. Atomically install without replacement when --force is false, or atomically replace the authorized destination entry when true; never truncate through a mutable final pathname. Apply exclusive unpredictable regular-file staging beside the authorized target to Python plan recording. Node recordPlan staging retains its separately established repair and identity. Expose/reuse native publication for Python CLI outputs with overwrite authorization passed into the commit operation; Node host publication must provide equivalent exclusive staging and atomic no-clobber/replacement. Preserve the documented final-output rule: forced publication replaces the selected symlink directory entry itself and leaves its referent unchanged; no-force installation must refuse an already occupied destination, including a dangling symlink.
Additional retained remediation detail: Use staged verified publication with held parent-directory authority for both wrappers. Carry overwrite authorization through commit and atomically refuse any existing destination when force is false; do not rely on a preliminary exists check.

findings.title: Rendering an admitted DOCX can retain gigabytes of duplicate embedded fonts
findings.summary: Distinct font-table aliases may all reference one embedded font part. Rendering eagerly loads every alias, copies the full font and retains a separate buffer for each name, multiplying a small admitted package into gigabytes of memory even if its body never uses those fonts. Assigned discovery-0031 corroborates distinct invented family names bypassing known-catalogue exclusions; valid Face::parse results and the later u16 face-index limit do not bound earlier alias copies.
findings.remediation:
Cache decoded font buffers by resolved package part and effective obfuscation key, share Arc values across aliases, and enforce an aggregate decoded-font allocation/work budget before copying.
Enforce face-count limits before decoding/retention and load only used faces where possible; cover all four style slots and different effective keys.

findings.title: Repeated relationship IDs trigger quadratic repair work
findings.summary: Opening a package repairs identical duplicate relationship IDs. For n distinct IDs each repeated identically, each repair linearly searches an increasingly long Vec, producing quadratic CPU work on shallow metadata that fits existing byte and attribute limits. Assigned discovery-0031 supplies approximately 200000 shallow Relationship records with 100000 distinct identical duplicate pairs within a 64 MiB part, implying about five billion membership comparisons. Conflicting duplicates remain promptly refused; counts are static.
findings.remediation: Track already-reported duplicate IDs in a HashSet or alongside seen-map state, retaining a Vec only for deterministic reporting order. Optionally cap relationship-record/work totals before repair; test many distinct identical duplicate pairs while preserving deterministic repaired-ID order and conflicting-duplicate refusals. Apply an active relationship-record/work budget at metadata admission in addition to making duplicate membership near-linear.

findings.title: Unbounded list levels cause billions of iterations or allocations
findings.summary:
Paragraph and numbering-definition ilvl attributes accept arbitrary u32 values. Resolving an undefined high level scans every lower integer; defining the high level instead drives counter initialization and label substitution loops over the same enormous range. Abstract definitions and full lvlOverride records accept the same unchecked level IDs; both missing-level reverse search and defined-level counter/label work require bounded handling.
 Assigned discovery-0032 preserves the valid numbering-instance prerequisite and the distinct billion-level defined-counter variant as well as undefined-level backwards search.
findings.remediation:
Validate the supported ilvl domain in paragraph, style, abstract and override sources before use. Find fallback levels among actual defined keys and initialize/substitute only supported or defined levels; avoid any iteration or allocation proportional to an untrusted numeric level. Return a typed refusal for unsupported level metadata rather than attempting dense counter or placeholder materialization.
Additional retained remediation detail: Validate paragraph and numbering-definition level IDs against the supported 0..=8 range. Resolve ancestors by actual defined keys and bound synthesized counters and marker iteration independently of untrusted integer values.

findings.title: Entity decoding repeatedly scans the input suffix
findings.summary: HTML altChunk text with bare ampersands and the public XML entity decoder repeatedly search the remaining suffix for ';', yielding quadratic CPU work. A valid admitted .rels Target containing repeated & is normalized upstream and redundantly decoded by PartFs, reaching the same XML sink during rendering, inspection, revision processing or comparison even when the target part does not exist. An additional admitted-main-XML route uses an unquoted value whose first character never reappears: the DOM consumes through EOF and decodes a bare-ampersand comment as an attribute, reaching the same quadratic XML decoder. Ordinary bare-ampersand text is rejected upstream and is not this proof. The same HTML decoder is also reached by Markdown-to-DOCX raw HTML blocks and attribute values; its ten-byte accepted-entity bound is applied after the unbounded search. Assigned discovery-0031 corroborates both established decoders independently: ordinary HTML/MHT paragraph text reaches the HTML helper even when script/style content is skipped, while an internal fontTable target reaches redundant XML decoding before any absent-part lookup. Its supplied offline dependency evidence identifies oxml-opc 0.14.2 and quick-xml 0.41.0 attribute normalization, independently supported by the repository target round-trip test. No reducer dependency inspection occurred.
findings.remediation: Scan entities once without revisiting suffixes. In HTML, bound the search to the supported entity-length window before looking for ';'; give XML decoding a monotonic parser or bounded entity grammar. Remove PartFs's redundant relationship decoding when upstream supplies normalized attributes; retain the linear XML-helper repair for its other callers and the separate bounded HTML-helper repair. Preserve canonical literal '&' part names and one-time entity normalization through round trips. Preserve the standalone XML helper's documented permissive output for unsupported or unterminated references while making its work linear. Apply practical relationship-target length/work bounds as defense in depth, preserving exactly one normalization pass and the standalone helper's linear permissive behavior. Align admission/DOM attribute token boundaries or reject unsupported unquoted syntax as defense in depth. Preserve the linear XML decoder fix for this comment-to-attribute route; removing only the redundant relationship decode does not cover it. Apply the bounded HTML helper consistently to Markdown raw-HTML block text and attribute consumers, using UTF-8-safe bounded lookahead and preserving recognized entities, malformed literal retention and multibyte text.

findings.title: Pull-request code runs on shared self-hosted infrastructure
findings.summary:
A lower-trust PR admitted to run can change a local action, build script, test or generator and execute it with self-hosted runner privileges. Four workflows share this missing isolation boundary; the local cache action documents private tokenless cache connectivity and reused checkout/disk. A permitted run also inherits the documented private Docker network and tokenless mbx-cache endpoint; cache poisoning, persistence and additional internal service access remain unverified deployment-dependent outcomes. Assigned discovery-0031 corroborates permitted fork execution across all four workflows and the documented tokenless private Docker cache network/reused checkouts. contents:read, persist-credentials:false and normal client-side PR cache-read policy do not establish process/network isolation. Actual approvals, worker lifecycle and server authorization remain unverified.
 Assigned discovery-0032 corroborates permitted fork execution in CI/docs/md-roundtrip/adoption and the documented private tokenless cache network, reused checkouts and persistent stores; actual approval, runner isolation and service authorization remain unverified.
findings.remediation:
Run lower-trust PR builds/tests/generators on GitHub-hosted or one-job disposable runners without trusted writable state or private infrastructure connectivity. Separate trusted main runners and enforce cache write authorization server-side. Apply consistently to ci, adoption, docs and md-roundtrip.
Additional retained remediation detail: Run untrusted PR jobs on GitHub-hosted or disposable isolated workers without trusted persistent stores/private services. Gate access to the shared self-hosted pool using trusted workflow logic outside PR control. Enforce cache read-only access at the service boundary when PRs need it.

findings.title: Python and Node plan recording can overwrite unrelated files through staging symlinks
findings.summary:
The Python and Node CLIs write plans through a predictable .<plan>.<PID>.partial pathname using nonexclusive truncating writes. A local actor who can create entries in the plan directory can preplace a symlink there and make the victim overwrite another file it can write, before the intended plan replacement.
 Assigned discovery-0032 corroborates both non-dry-run recorders after successful plan preview. Intentional final-plan symlink resolution is distinct from the independently substituted staging entry.
findings.remediation:
Use exclusive, unpredictable staging owned by a private directory, hold the opened handle through writing, and rename that verified file. Reuse the native publication design or equivalent mkstemp/exclusive wx APIs and never follow existing staging entries. Python can reuse native publication; Node needs equivalent secure publication semantics. Preserve intentional final-plan symlink resolution to its authorized resolved target while securing the separate staging object; successful recording installs a verified regular plan file and failure preserves prior output.
Additional retained remediation detail: Use an exclusively created private staging directory/file held by handle, verify staged bytes, and atomically publish to the authorized plan target. Refuse preexisting staging objects and preserve intended final-plan symlink semantics without following a staging symlink.

findings.title: PDF generation can hang on a font with many retained tables
findings.summary:
An embedded TrueType font with at least 32768 retained directory records reaches a u16 doubling loop while its PDF subset is written. Normal release arithmetic wraps the loop state to zero and never terminates; overflow-checked builds panic.
 Assigned discovery-0032 supplies duplicate allowlisted name records as an alternative to the established duplicate cvt-space framing, with roughly 512 KiB of directory records at the threshold; usable selected non-catalogue glyf faces and used text remain required.
findings.remediation:
Reject duplicate sfnt tags and unreasonable table counts, calculate search metadata in a wider checked integer type, and refuse unrepresentable header values before looping.
Additional retained remediation detail: Reject duplicate font table tags and cap retained table count to the distinct supported set. Compute sfnt search metadata with checked wider arithmetic and return a controlled error for invalid counts.

findings.title: PDF font subsetting can enumerate billions of codepoints
findings.summary:
An embedded TrueType font with a compact format12 or format13 cmap range ending at u32::MAX can make PDF conversion perform about 4.29 billion callbacks. The converter only keeps BMP entries, but filters them after the unbounded enumeration.
 Assigned discovery-0032 preserves Windows platform 3/encoding 10 format13 acceptance and the inclusive full-u32 group: 4294967296 callbacks. Tuple evaluation also performs glyph lookup when u16 conversion fails.
findings.remediation:
Generate the BMP subset by bounded codepoint lookup or explicitly intersect and budget ranges before enumeration. Bound cumulative iteration across subtables, including overlapping ranges.
Additional retained remediation detail: Enumerate the bounded output codepoint domain directly, or intersect encoded ranges with it before enumeration. Bound aggregate mappings/work across subtables and reject invalid or excessive ranges before callbacks.

findings.title: HTML selector groups multiply CSS values into excessive memory
findings.summary: A DOCX HTML altChunk can combine one large CSS property value with thousands of grouped selectors. The importer deep-copies the complete property map into each selector, consuming gigabytes even if none of the rules are used. A supplied framing uses 4096 distinct selectors and one 1 MiB value for about 4 GiB of retained value storage, excluding overhead; this is a static estimate. Additional supplied static framing: 10000 distinct short selectors sharing a 1 MiB property imply about 10 GiB of retained values from approximately 1.1 MiB HTML; this is not a memory measurement.
findings.remediation: Share immutable declaration maps/values across grouped selectors and enforce cumulative selector, rule and declaration-byte budgets before allocation. Enforce value-length limits and discard unsupported properties before retaining them; unused selectors and properties must still count toward the aggregate budget.

findings.title: Crafted MATH metrics can expand an equation into excessive glyphs
findings.summary: A document with a crafted embedded math font can make inline fractions increase font size instead of reducing it. An enclosing stretchy delimiter then computes a huge extender count and stores one glyph per repetition, exhausting rendering resources despite shallow XML nesting. The assigned radical variant supplies finite arithmetic: unitsPerEm=1000, leaf yMax=1000, scriptPercentScaleDown=10000 (factor 100), ten nested inline numerator fractions at 12 pt, and one radical extender with fullAdvance=1 and zero overlap. The derived target/advance exceeds 1e23 and saturates to usize::MAX before the glyph loop. This is a supplied static construction, with no crafted-font acceptance or runtime demonstration.
findings.remediation: Validate MATH scale percentages and metrics against supported finite ranges; reject extreme geometry and enforce a cumulative assembly-glyph budget before converting ratios to counts or allocating. Enforce hard per-assembly repetition caps as well as aggregate glyph bounds before floating-point-to-usize casts, and cover both unmarked radicals and delimiters with small positive extender advance above overlap.

Use the same decoding across leak checks and package validation.

findings.title: Rendering an HTML chunk can allocate gigabytes from a single colspan value
findings.summary: A document author can place a huge positive colspan in a small embedded HTML/MHT altChunk table. Ordinary DOCX rendering generates one grid XML element per effective column after original package admission and before DOM/layout checks. A count of 1000000000 drives a billion appends; 4294967295 generates over 85 GB of markup, exhausting CPU/memory. The supplied positive 4294967295 framing fits both 32-bit and 64-bit usize and needs no arithmetic overflow. Assigned discovery-0031 corroborates colspan=1000000000 causing tens of gigabytes of generated XML and work before layout; rejecting invalid, negative or zero spans does not bound valid positive values.
findings.remediation: Enforce a practical maximum cell span and checked per-row/aggregate column counts before generating any table XML. Charge all HTML/MHT-generated WML, including repeated/nested tables, to a cumulative byte/work budget inside altChunk expansion and return a typed input-limit refusal before allocation or DOM construction.

findings.title: WMF record-boundary failures amplify polygon work and retained text
findings.summary: Rendering a DOCX with a crafted placeable WMF lets short declared records consume payload from later records, which the outer parser then revisits. Polygon/polypolygon/polyline records can cause billions of coordinate decodes from roughly 512 KiB; EXTTEXTOUT/TEXTOUT records can retain hundreds of megabytes of overlapping owned strings from roughly 205.6 KB. The common missing record-local boundary bypasses the canvas cap and original package budgets. A further framing uses alternating six-byte EXTTEXTOUT and unknown 0xFFFF record headers to claim 65,535 text bytes from subsequent records, implying several GiB of retained strings from roughly 1 MiB of media; this is a static estimate. A supplied 7-word EXTTEXTOUT framing uses 65536 fourteen-byte records plus a 65535-byte suffix in less than 1 MiB and requests about 4 GiB of decoded characters; nonzero mapping dimensions and nonblank text are required. This is a static estimate. Assigned discovery-0031 supplies an additional static eight-byte TEXTOUT framing with a 65535-byte claimed string and overlapping following bytes. About 1 MiB can request multiple gigabytes of retained text; valid whole-file reads, nonblank text and nonzero mapping extents remain required. No out-of-bounds memory read is asserted.
findings.remediation: Confine every WMF handler, including field, font, string and geometry reads, to a slice limited to its checked declared record extent. Before allocation validate fixed fields, ring/point counts and coordinate arrays, EXTTEXTOUT options/optional rectangle and text count, and TEXTOUT padded string plus trailing coordinates against that slice using checked arithmetic. Refuse inconsistent records before decoding/rasterization/replay and enforce cumulative decoded-text, record and total geometry/work budgets. Keep the already bounded EMF behavior.

findings.title: Entity decoding repeatedly scans the input suffix
findings.summary: HTML altChunk text with bare ampersands and the public XML entity decoder repeatedly search the remaining suffix for ';', yielding quadratic CPU work. A valid admitted .rels Target containing repeated & is normalized upstream and redundantly decoded by PartFs, reaching the same XML sink during rendering, inspection, revision processing or comparison even when the target part does not exist. An additional admitted-main-XML route uses an unquoted value whose first character never reappears: the DOM consumes through EOF and decodes a bare-ampersand comment as an attribute, reaching the same quadratic XML decoder. Ordinary bare-ampersand text is rejected upstream and is not this proof. The same HTML decoder is also reached by Markdown-to-DOCX raw HTML blocks and attribute values; its ten-byte accepted-entity bound is applied after the unbounded search. Assigned discovery-0031 corroborates both established decoders independently: ordinary HTML/MHT paragraph text reaches the HTML helper even when script/style content is skipped, while an internal fontTable target reaches redundant XML decoding before any absent-part lookup. Its supplied offline dependency evidence identifies oxml-opc 0.14.2 and quick-xml 0.41.0 attribute normalization, independently supported by the repository target round-trip test. No reducer dependency inspection occurred.
findings.remediation: Scan entities once without revisiting suffixes. In HTML, bound the search to the supported entity-length window before looking for ';'; give XML decoding a monotonic parser or bounded entity grammar. Remove PartFs's redundant relationship decoding when upstream supplies normalized attributes; retain the linear XML-helper repair for its other callers and the separate bounded HTML-helper repair. Preserve canonical literal '&' part names and one-time entity normalization through round trips. Preserve the standalone XML helper's documented permissive output for unsupported or unterminated references while making its work linear. Apply practical relationship-target length/work bounds as defense in depth, preserving exactly one normalization pass and the standalone helper's linear permissive behavior. Align admission/DOM attribute token boundaries or reject unsupported unquoted syntax as defense in depth. Preserve the linear XML decoder fix for this comment-to-attribute route; removing only the redundant relationship decode does not cover it. Apply the bounded HTML helper consistently to Markdown raw-HTML block text and attribute consumers, using UTF-8-safe bounded lookahead and preserving recognized entities, malformed literal retention and multibyte text.

findings.title: Pull-request code runs on shared self-hosted infrastructure
findings.summary: A lower-trust PR admitted to run can change a local action, build script, test or generator and execute it with self-hosted runner privileges. Four workflows share this missing isolation boundary; the local cache action documents private tokenless cache connectivity and reused checkout/disk. A permitted run also inherits the documented private Docker network and tokenless mbx-cache endpoint; cache poisoning, persistence and additional internal service access remain unverified deployment-dependent outcomes. Assigned discovery-0031 corroborates permitted fork execution across all four workflows and the documented tokenless private Docker cache network/reused checkouts. contents:read, persist-credentials:false and normal client-side PR cache-read policy do not establish process/network isolation. Actual approvals, worker lifecycle and server authorization remain unverified.
findings.remediation: Run lower-trust PR builds/tests/generators on GitHub-hosted or one-job disposable runners without trusted writable state or private infrastructure connectivity. Separate trusted main runners and enforce cache write authorization server-side. Apply consistently to ci, adoption, docs and md-roundtrip.
